body.statement: For either two-score mode and every feasible branch, \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{arr}}\) returns the same endpoint as the primal LP and the unrestricted cone dual after \(O(|\mathcal M_a|^2)\) candidate intersections and \(O(|\mathcal M_a|^3)\) naive arithmetic per endpoint. A separate LP computes \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\); primal infeasibility or a dual recession ray certifies an empty branch. The statement includes parallel kink lines, zero scores, tied optima, and structural-zero cells removed before forming \(\mathcal J\).
body.justification: Exact branch and endpoint certificates are essential near the zero-slack boundary.
body.gap: Generic LP solvers compute values but do not expose this two-score finite certificate or prevent finite-multiplier confusion with infeasibility.
body.consumer: A production implementation can certify the early-kill cases \(\varepsilon=-0.001,0,0.001\) without ad hoc tolerances changing the population target.
body.proof_tex:
For a fixed branch, primal feasibility is a finite linear feasibility problem over \(|\mathcal M_a|\) box variables and two score inequalities.  The slack value is a second finite linear program over \((x_a,t_a)\), exactly as displayed in \(\text{def:interior-slack}\).  Thus feasibility and \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\) have ordinary primal certificates and, when the numerical inputs are rational, exact rational certificates.

For a feasible branch, \(\text{thm:cone-endpoint-sharpness}\) shows that the appropriate cone dual is finite and attained.  Each summand in either dual switches affine formula only when
\[
 1-b\lambda's_j^r=0
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 1+b\lambda's_j^r=0,                                                           \tag{42}
\]
respectively.  Together with \(\lambda_1=0\) and \(\lambda_2=0\), these lines partition \(\mathbb R_+^2\) into finitely many polyhedral cells.  On the closure of every cell the dual objective is affine.  Every such cell is pointed because it is contained in the nonnegative quadrant.  If a finite affine optimum occurs in a cell interior, either a direction improves the value until a boundary is reached or the objective is constant in that direction; repeating in two dimensions reaches a vertex without changing the optimum.  If the maximizing or minimizing face is an unbounded ray, finiteness rules out improvement along the ray, and moving to its finite endpoint again gives a vertex optimum.  Every vertex is the nonnegative intersection of two linearly independent boundary lines, with the origin included.  Hence \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{arr}}\) returns the same value as the dual and therefore the primal LP.

With \(m=|\mathcal M_a|\), there are at most \(m+2\) relevant lines and hence \(O(m^2)\) pairs.  Evaluating a dual objective takes \(O(m)\) arithmetic operations, giving \(O(m^3)\) naive arithmetic per endpoint.  Parallel lines simply yield no linearly independent intersection; a zero score creates no kink because its summand is globally affine; tied optima are harmless because only one optimal vertex is needed.

For completeness, infeasibility has a distinct certificate.  Let
\(G=\{b(h_a^r+\sum_jp_js_j^rx_j):x\in\prod_j[\ell_a,u_a]\}\).  This compact convex set is disjoint from \(\mathbb R_+^2\) exactly when the branch is empty.  Choose closest points \(g_0\in G\) and \(z_0\in\mathbb R_+^2\), and put \(\lambda=z_0-g_0\).  The two projection inequalities give
\[
 \lambda\ge0,\qquad \lambda'z_0=0,\qquad
 \sup_{g\in G}\lambda'g\le-\|z_0-g_0\|^2<0.                                 \tag{43}
\]
Scaling \(\lambda\) in the lower dual sends its value to \(+\infty\), while scaling it in the upper dual sends its value to \(-\infty\).  Thus (43) is a recession certificate of emptiness and cannot be confused with failure to find a finite multiplier.  Finally, structural-zero cells are absent from \(\mathcal J\) by \(\text{ass:finite-grid}\); the preceding arguments require neither general position nor unique optima.  This proves all asserted degeneracy cases and complexity bounds.
